concepts.name: 回声海螺
concepts.title: I  HELIX AUDITOR
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Premium original retro-futurist mechanical desktop sculpture concept sheet for MagicDesk. Cream glazed porcelain, polished nickel and dark brushed steel, tiny oxide-red hardware, precision pivots, restrained amber/red light, excellent industrial detailing, clean materials without heavy grime. Grounded believable connected mechanical assemblies with visible axles. A single shared low circular HELIOS pedestal in every view: stepped dark metal rim, ivory curved front control fascia, a unique model-specific physical control cassette inside the front fascia, different button count and shapes for this machine, with a clearly separated red X exit at far right, circular top mounting socket; same diameter and height. Pedestal design must remain extremely close to the supplied reference. No levitating base, no game controller, no screen or UI overlay, no left/right selection arrows, no blue-purple neon, no magic runes. Neutral charcoal studio background and realistic studio render lighting. This is a visual design proposal, not a finished model. Wide 3:2 detailed board: large hero view occupying left 60%, top-right action view, bottom-right coherent exploded assembly view. Same object and same pedestal across views, full object visible without clipping. Small elegant cream condensed headings. Text only the exact title and 'REST', 'ACTIVE', 'ASSEMBLY'.
Art direction explicitly references Atomic Heart: Soviet retro-futurist biotechnology and precision experimental laboratory machinery, milk-white sculptural porcelain, chrome mechanical anatomy, dark steel and red enamel. Design an original object, not a recreation of an existing game asset. Keep the SAME shared pedestal outer shell/diameter/proportions in all views, but give this model its OWN functional physical controls. Visible joints and mechanical continuity must be consistent across REST, ACTIVE and ASSEMBLY. All parts attach to the pedestal through a visible mount, never floating.
Replace the egg above the reference pedestal with HELIX AUDITOR, an uncanny acoustic listening machine shaped like a thick elegant asymmetrical SPIRAL CONCH. Body consists of six broad curved ivory ceramic armor segments following one continuous spiral nickel spine. A broad flared acoustic mouth contains concentric perforated metal diaphragms and tiny red ceramic tuning-fork elements; dark articulated supports visibly connect it to the socket. Not a gramophone with a straight horn, not a humanoid face. REST: segments overlap tightly, the mouth partially shuttered, spiral leans inquisitively left. ACTIVE: the six armor segments peel outward sequentially along their attached hinge links like a spiral unfolding, exposing continuous coiled chrome ribs; diaphragm lamellae flex concentrically and a few fine amber sound contours form immediately around the mouth. Remains on its mount. ASSEMBLY: shell segments, diaphragms and tuning forks separate along their assembly axes, with the coiled inner spine and base visible and connected. Controls in fascia: one LARGE ridged tuning dial, one short curved throat-shutter lever and two small different shaped pulse tabs, not seven circles. Visually convey a listening/singing kinetic sculpture with a volumetric spiral silhouette. Exact title 'I  HELIX AUDITOR'.

Replace the egg above the reference pedestal with MERCURY HERBARIUM, a strange biomimetic laboratory bonsai made entirely of porcelain, nickel joints and sealed red liquid capillaries. A gracefully offset ivory trunk has THREE chrome articulated branches, each ending in one different-height cream ceramic bud; six delicate rigid leaf plates with perforated vein structures on short hinge stems. Thin transparent red capillary tubes visibly follow the branches. REST: trunk telescoped low, three buds folded into smooth teardrop capsules, leaves close to branches, miniature experimental botanical specimen. ACTIVE: telescoping trunk segments extend, three branches unfold from elbow hinges, the THREE buds open into precise small ceramic-petal calyxes around slender red glass pistils, leaves tilt toward light sequentially. No central spherical sun, no actual organic plant matter, no flying spores cloud. Tiny contained red liquid pulses and restrained amber indicator glows. ASSEMBLY: exactly three complete flower/bud cartridges lift from their branch sockets, leaf plates and trunk cladding offset from their pins, branching nickel skeleton and tubes stay understandable. Own controls: three bud-shaped ivory rocker keys, an irrigation-style pump lever and one small ribbed pulse dial. It is a biomechanical botanical instrument, not an ordinary plant in a pot. Exact title 'J  MERCURY HERBARIUM'.

Replace the egg above the reference base with ASTROGRAPH SCRIBE, a LOW WIDE retrofuture star-chart engraving automaton. An oblong ivory ceramic clam-shell housing contains two distinct horizontal nickel tape reels at left and right, a continuous narrow smoked-metal ribbon passing between them over a supported platen, and THREE fine articulated engraving arms like elegant mechanical typebars mounted to a visible rear crossbeam. All attached to a short gimbal on the same circular pedestal; upper machine is wide and squat, never tall egg-shaped. REST: curved porcelain hood closed except for the ribbon inspection slit and one small analog calibration dial. ACTIVE: two hood halves slide sideways and tilt up on visible four-bar linkages, three stylus arms dance in different phases over the ribbon, engraving tiny amber constellation points and hair-thin connecting lines on the physically supported strip. Ribbon winds from one reel to the other without levitating. ASSEMBLY: two reel cartridges lift along their axles, the three complete stylus modules separate from the crossbeam, covers offset outward; show coherent tape threading path and base remains intact. Unique fascia controls: three short ivory typewriter-like keys, a side carriage-return lever and a serrated feed thumbwheel, no repeated seven circle buttons. No laptop screen, no readable generated prose on ribbon, no handheld gun. Exact title 'K  ASTROGRAPH SCRIBE'.

Replace the egg above the reference pedestal with TRIPHASE OBSERVATORY, a curious anchored optical machine with exactly THREE independently moving periscope heads. A low smooth ivory kidney-shaped carapace supports three retractable nickel necks in staggered positions; each neck contains clearly segmented telescoping tubes plus TWO visible pivot joints, and ends in a small porcelain oval lens housing with a precise mechanical iris and red-amber optical reflections. One head short and broad, one medium, one tall and slender; same family but not three identical cameras. REST: necks partly retracted, heads cluster together and look in subtly different directions, no human face or eyeballs. ACTIVE: necks extend to different heights and pivot outward, then their irises orient toward a single small amber optical target suspended by two thin real supporting wires between the heads; three narrow beams briefly intersect there. Heads connected at all times; looks like inquisitive laboratory biotechnical creature, not a security camera rig, robot drone or weapon. ASSEMBLY: exactly three whole head cartridges and telescoping neck sections separate along their real shafts above the same intact carapace and pedestal. Unique control cassette: three differently notched lens-selector rocker switches, one long ridged focus roller and a small iris lever with a curved slot. Keep common separate red X. Exact title 'L  TRIPHASE OBSERVATORY'.
